objectives: Perform immediate post-convulsion danger-sign assessment in a febrile child.
Differentiate likely simple febrile convulsion from meningitis danger pattern.
Choose stabilization, investigation, and referral actions appropriate to findings.
takeaways: History of convulsion is a high-risk signal until danger signs are excluded.
Alert child with no neck stiffness, no repeated convulsions, and good oral intake may be managed with close observation.
Any persistent altered consciousness, recurrent seizure, or meningeal signs needs urgent referral.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A mother brings her 2-year-old after a fever-related convulsion at home. Decide rapidly between safe observation and urgent escalation.

sections.title: Event history
sections.text: Seizure lasted about 2 minutes, stopped spontaneously before arrival.

coach.title: Grace is sleepy but arousable
coach.body: Immediate danger-sign reassessment is more important than routine queue workflow.

sections.title: Neurologic danger signs
sections.reveal_note: None currently present; child now responsive and drinking.

coach.title: How should you interpret this status?
coach.body: Choose the safest classification after current exam.

question.prompt: What is the best immediate interpretation?

options.text: Post-febrile convulsion, currently stable but requires close monitoring and cause evaluation
Psychogenic event, no fever management needed

question.right: Correct. Child had a convulsion, so careful observation and fever source assessment are still required even if danger signs are absent now.
question.wrong: Either overcalling without evidence or early discharge is unsafe. Post-seizure children need structured reassessment.

sections.title: Current neuro exam
sections.text: Alert, no neck stiffness, no repeat convulsion in facility.

coach.title: Choose the most appropriate next action
coach.body: Combine positive findings with current stability.

options.text: Treat confirmed febrile illness per guideline, observe closely, and counsel immediate return if seizure recurs
Ignore fever source since seizure already stopped
Discharge without counseling once child is awake
Give sedatives for home use to prevent all future convulsions

question.right: Correct. Current exam does not show meningitis danger signs, so treat identified febrile cause, observe, and provide strict seizure return precautions.
question.wrong: Stopping at seizure cessation misses ongoing risk. Care must include cause-directed treatment and caregiver safety-netting.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You stabilized and reassessed a post-convulsion child, then matched management to current danger-sign status.
sections.emphasis: Structured neurologic screening prevented unsafe assumptions.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: Fever with convulsion demands high vigilance. When repeat seizures, neck stiffness, persistent altered consciousness, or inability to drink appear, urgent referral is required.
